defs.d: The act of doing that which begins anything; commencement of an action, state, or space of time; entrance into being or upon a course; the first act, effort, or state of a succession of acts or states.
That which is begun; a rudiment or element.
Water in frozen (solid) form.
Any frozen volatile chemical, such as ammonia or carbon dioxide.
To cool with ice, as a beverage.
To become ice; to freeze.
A person who serves as a subject for artwork or fashion, usually in the medium of photography but also for painting or drawing.
defs.ex: The beautiful model had her face on the cover of almost every fashion magazine imaginable.

defs.d: A person, usually an attractive female, hired to show items or goods to the public, such as items given away as prizes on a TV game show.
To display for others to see, especially in regard to wearing clothing while performing the role of a fashion model
defs.ex: She modelled the shoes for her friends to see.

defs.d: To use as an object in the creation of a forecast or model
defs.ex: They modelled the data with a computer to analyze the experiment’s results.

defs.d: Worthy of being a model; exemplary.
A unary operation on logical values that changes true to false, and false to true.
Negates the meaning of the modified verb.
defs.ex: Did you take out the trash? No, I did not.

defs.d: To no degree.
defs.ex: It's not you, it's me.

defs.d: And not.
defs.ex: He painted the car blue and black, not solid purple.

defs.d: A difficulty that has to be resolved or dealt with.
defs.ex: She's leaving because she faced numerous problems to do with racism.

defs.d: A question to be answered, schoolwork exercise.
(of a person or an animal) Difficult to train or guide; unruly.
Causing a problem; problematic; troublesome.

A reflexive, often habitual behavior, especially one occurring in a context that often features attempts at deception by persons under psychological stress (such as a poker game or police interrogation), that reveals information that the person exhibiting the behavior is attempting to withhold.
That which is told; a tale or account.
(archaic outside of idioms) To count, reckon, or enumerate.
defs.ex: All told, there were over a dozen.  Can you tell time on a clock?  He had untold wealth.

defs.d: To narrate.
defs.ex: I want to tell a story;  I want to tell you a story.

defs.d: A sport played by two players (or four in doubles), who alternately strike the ball over a net using racquets.
A match in this sport.
To play tennis.
To drive backward and forward like a tennis ball.
A solar year, the time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).
defs.ex: we moved to this town a year ago;  I quit smoking exactly one year ago

defs.d: (by extension) The time it takes for any astronomical object (such as a planet, dwarf planet, small Solar System body, or comet) in direct orbit around a star (such as the Sun) to make one revolution around the star.
defs.ex: Mars goes around the sun once in a Martian year, or 1.88 Earth years.

defs.d: Exposure to likely harm; peril.
defs.ex: There's plenty of danger in the desert.

defs.d: An instance or cause of likely harm.
To claim liability.
To imperil; to endanger.
A person who designs something, or who designs things as a profession.
A plotter or schemer.
Created by a designer, especially a fashion designer.
defs.ex: a designer briefcase

defs.d: An act of being of assistance to someone.
defs.ex: I say I did him a service by ending our relationship – now he can freely pursue his career.

defs.d: The practice of providing such a service as economic activity.
defs.ex: Hair care is a service industry.

defs.d: To serve.
defs.ex: They service the customer base.

defs.d: To perform maintenance.
defs.ex: He is going to service the car.

defs.d: A very tall iron-framed structure, usually painted red and white, on which microwave, radio, satellite, or other communication antennas are installed; mast.
A similarly framed structure with a platform or enclosed area on top, used as a lookout for spotting fires, plane crashes, fugitives, etc.
A cohesive whole built up of distinct parts.
defs.ex: The birds had built an amazing structure out of sticks and various discarded items.

defs.d: The underlying shape of a solid.
defs.ex: He studied the structure of her face.

defs.d: To give structure to; to arrange.
defs.ex: I'm trying to structure my time better so I'm not always late.

defs.d: The act of arriving or something that has arrived.
defs.ex: The early arrival of the bride created a stir.

defs.d: The attainment of an objective, especially as a result of effort.
defs.ex: The arrival of the railway made the local tourist industry viable.

defs.d: Prohibition.
A public proclamation or edict; a summons by public proclamation. Chiefly, in early use, a summons to arms.
defs.ex: Bans is common and ordinary amongst the Feudists, and signifies a proclamation, or any public notice.

defs.d: To summon; to call out.
To anathematize; to pronounce an ecclesiastical curse upon; to place under a ban.
The method by which a device performs its function.
The method or practice by which actions are done.
Endowed with one or more talents.
To relate or belong to; to have reference to or connection with; to affect the interest of; to be of importance to.
To engage by feeling or sentiment; to interest.
defs.ex: A good prince concerns himself in the happiness of his subjects.

defs.d: Showing concern.
defs.ex: There was a concerned expression on her face as I told her the news.

defs.d: Involved or responsible.
defs.ex: The people concerned have been punished.

defs.d: Spanning the world; global.
defs.ex: A large meteorite impact would cause worldwide extinction of life.

defs.d: Throughout the world.
defs.ex: English is spoken worldwide.

defs.d: To consider carefully; to weigh well in the mind.
defs.ex: It is now time for the jury to deliberate the guilt of the defendant.

defs.d: To consider the reasons for and against anything; to reflect.
Done on purpose; intentional.
defs.ex: Tripping me was deliberate action.

defs.d: Of a person, weighing facts and arguments with a view to a choice or decision; carefully considering the probable consequences of a step; slow in determining.
defs.ex: The jury took eight hours to come to its deliberate verdict.

defs.d: A machine or device that converts other energy forms into mechanical energy, or imparts motion.
A motor car, or automobile.
defs.ex: Nice motor!

defs.d: To make a journey by motor vehicle; to drive.
defs.ex: On Saturday we motored down to Plymouth.

defs.d: To move at a brisk pace.
defs.ex: Sales were slow at first, but now things are really motoring.

defs.d: Relating to the ability to move
defs.ex: She has excellent motor skills.

defs.d: Relating to motor cars
defs.ex: Motor insurance is expensive for youngsters.

defs.d: An elderly person
(the elderly) older people as a whole
Old; having lived for relatively many years.
Of an object, being old-fashioned or frail due to aging.
Someone who is an expert in, or devoted to, some specific branch of study or research.
A physician whose practice is limited to a particular branch of medicine or surgery.
Specialised.
The study of the human mind.
The study of human behavior.
